summary: LS_XSESSION.sh is now a small supervisor that owns the dedicated session. Fluxbox and the D-Bus session run for the whole session, and Fluxbox is started again if it ends. Graphite's window is the supervisor's child. After an unexpected end (any status other than 0) it is started again after a wait of 2, 4 or 8 s (at most 30 s), at most 3 times in a row. After that the session ends at the text console with a plain message, which START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh prints. Status 0 (Return to Debian, or the close after Log out, Restart or Shut down) ends the session. A workspace or look switch hands the start over to the supervisor, so the session goes on. The new workbench/session_launch.py is the one launch path for apps: a short-lived helper starts the program with setsid, so the app is not Graphite's child and survives a Graphite crash. session_power.py adds Lock and Suspend. Lock starts xsecurelock in a session of its own and counts only when xsecurelock confirms the lock; with no locker it gives a plain reason. Suspend uses logind CanSuspend and Suspend, with the lock taken and confirmed first: no lock, no suspend. session_power.py also adds availability() over the six actions, sleep_held (logind Inhibit 'sleep', delay mode, around her staged writes) and, in the dedicated session, SleepGuard (locks before any sleep and on logind's Lock signal). The System menu and the File menu's leave group read Lock, Suspend, Log out, Restart, Shut down, Return to Debian.

existing_tests_changed: tests_integrated/test_startup_scripts.py: the three LS_XSESSION.sh runs with a non-zero stand-in status now pass ARC_LEDGER_SESSION_RESTART_LIMIT=0. The supervisor now starts Graphite again after a non-zero exit, so the test's 'office runs once and its status is passed on' holds only with restarts turned off.

tests_integrated/test_system_menu.py: FakeLogind now answers CanSuspend and the locker look-up (no locker installed). The no-session and darwin assertions cover only the logind actions: Lock needs no logind, the leave row is always available, and the locker look-up is not a logind request. The menu's words, captions and reasons follow the new order, with Lock and Suspend. End now reaches the leave row (the last row), and Up from there reaches Shut down. The 'refused before anything else' check ignores the menu's own locker look-up.
decisions: The supervisor is bash inside LS_XSESSION.sh, not Python, so the session still starts when Graphite's Python environment is broken. Exit 0 counts as an intended end; any other status, or a signal, counts as unexpected. Settings: ARC_LEDGER_SESSION_RESTART_LIMIT (3), ARC_LEDGER_SESSION_BACKOFF (2 s, doubled each time, at most 30 s) and ARC_LEDGER_SESSION_STABLE (a run of 120 s or more starts the count afresh). Each start and end is a line in session.log; last-session.json now also records restarts and message.

The plan did not cover Graphite starting itself again on a workspace or look switch (shell2.relaunch). Before, relaunch started a detached window and then exited 0; under the supervisor that exit would have ended the session and killed the new window. In the supervised session relaunch now writes a hand-over request carrying only ARC_LEDGER_, ARC1_ and GRAPHITE_ settings, and the supervisor starts Graphite again at once. This does not count as a crash. Outside the supervised session nothing changes.

The launch path detaches through a short-lived Python helper: the helper starts the program with start_new_session, then exits. This avoids os.fork in the threaded Qt process and does not need Qt. The program is reparented away, so it is not in Graphite's descendant tree either. Graphite's own settings and the PySide and venv variables are taken out of its environment.

Existing program starts were left alone. The programs.* Kernel operations already use start_new_session, and Calc already uses QProcess.startDetached. Re-routing them would get around the tests' holds on those calls. S2 should use session_launch.launch.

Lock starts xsecurelock directly as `xsecurelock -- touch <mark>`, and the lock counts only when the mark appears. For 'logind LockSession', Graphite listens to logind's Lock signal for its own session (SleepGuard), so loginctl lock-session and logind's own requests lock through the same locker. Graphite does not call LockSession itself, because that would only send the request back to Graphite.

Lock and Suspend have no confirmation dialog, because they close nothing. Suspend first saves Graphite's session, then takes the lock, then asks logind, and it is refused if the lock is not confirmed. Without a locker, Suspend is unavailable and says why. The dedicated session's 'challenge' rule (no permission agent there) applies to Suspend as it does to Restart.

SleepGuard goes beyond the slice text: it holds a delay inhibitor and listens for PrepareForSleep, so a lid-close or idle suspend also locks first. Where it cannot listen it holds nothing, so it never delays a suspend for nothing.
sleep_held is wired into SlateFace.run_staged, the one place where her changes are dispatched.
The System menu's foot caption changed from 'each asks first and keeps your work' to 'each keeps your work; leaving asks first', because Lock and Suspend ask nothing.
The new on-screen words say 'apps', never 'Programs'. The new row icons are a padlock (Lock) and a crescent (Suspend). An unavailable row keeps the word '· unavailable' beside its quiet ink.
findings_for_the_coordinator: From memory of xsecurelock's documentation, it runs the command after '--' once the screen is locked. xsecurelock is not installed here, so a stand-in was used. Check this on the ThinkPad. If the memory is wrong, Lock reports 'not confirmed' and Suspend refuses, which is the safe failure.

S5: start lxpolkit in LS_XSESSION.sh next to Fluxbox, before the loop. Then relax session_power's 'challenge is unavailable in the dedicated session' rule (NO_PROMPT) for Restart, Shut down and Suspend.
S2 must start apps through session_launch.launch(argv, cwd, name). S3 can use session_launch.launched() (process id checked against its start time) to mark the windows Graphite started.
K1 and K2: wrap each file-writing step in session_power.sleep_held(why).

This one predates S1, for K3 (HALT): Stop all jobs (qt_master_stop) kills Graphite's descendants by parent id. Program windows started by the existing programs.* operations are among them: they use Popen with start_new_session but are still direct children. Starting them through session_launch.launch would keep them out.
The leave flow does not yet warn about open apps that will close with the session at Return to Debian. S3's window list could make that possible.
No registry change: S1 adds no Kernel operations, and the regenerated docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json was identical. The patch applies to a clean HEAD checkout (git apply --check).
not_done: Nothing was tested in the owner's sense, and nothing ran on the ThinkPad, a real X server, real logind, real xsecurelock or a real suspend. The checks used stand-ins: bash stubs, a stand-in xsecurelock, and a stand-in logind on a private D-Bus.
Return to Debian does not close open apps politely; they close when the X server goes.
There is no polkit agent in the session yet (S5).
release_note: The session survives Graphite. In the dedicated Debian session a small supervisor keeps Fluxbox and the session bus running for the whole session. If Graphite's window ends unexpectedly, the supervisor starts it again, waiting a little longer each time, at most three times in a row; after that it returns to the text console with a plain message. Apps opened from Graphite run on their own and stay open meanwhile. The session group gains Lock (xsecurelock) and Suspend (the screen is locked first, then the computer sleeps), and now reads Lock, Suspend, Log out, Restart, Shut down, Return to Debian. A suspend waits until a file Kasandra is writing is done. Built, not tested: only the ThinkPad can prove it.
